name: Question 15
problem: The price $P(t)$ of a particular good varies according to the differential equation ${P}^{′}(t)=rP(t),$ where $t$ is the time, measured in years, and $r>0.$ It is known that the price of the good tripled after the first six years. How long did it take for the price to double from the initial price?
worked_solution:
The general solution to the given differential equation is

$$
P(t)={P}_{0}{e}^{rt},
$$

where ${P}_{0}$ is the price of the good when $t=0.$

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the price equals $2{P}_{0}.$ Then, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P({t}_{1}) & =2{P}_{0}\,⇒\,{P}_{0}{e}^{r{t}_{1}}=2{P}_{0}.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve this equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{0}{e}^{r{t}_{1}} & =2{P}_{0} \\ \cancel{{P}_{0}}{e}^{r{t}_{1}} & =2\cancel{{P}_{0}} \\ {e}^{r{t}_{1}} & =2 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{r{t}_{1}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ r{t}_{1} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{r}\,\,(∗)\end{aligned}
$$

We now need to calculate $r.$ We're told that the price of the good tripled after the first six years. Therefore,

$$
P(6)=3{P}_{0}\,⇒\,{P}_{0}{e}^{6r}=3{P}_{0}.
$$

We solve this equation for $r,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{0}{e}^{6r} & =3{P}_{0} \\ \cancel{{P}_{0}}{e}^{6r} & =3\cancel{{P}_{0}} \\ {e}^{6r} & =3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{6r}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ r & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this into $(∗)$ and evaluating, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{r} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{6})} \\  & =\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & ≈3.8,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.

html:
Question 15
?

The price P(t) of a particular good varies according to the differential equation P′(t)=rP(t), where t is the time, measured in years, and r>0. It is known that the price of the good tripled after the first six years. How long did it take for the price to double from the initial price?

a
3.1 years
b
3.4 years
c
3.2 years
d
3.5 years
e
3.8 years
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The general solution to the given differential equation is P(t)=P0ert, where P0 is the price of the good when t=0.

Let t1 be the time when the price equals 2P0. Then, we have P(t1)=2P0⇒P0ert1=2P0.

We solve this equation for t1, as follows: P0ert1=2P0P0ert1=2P0ert1=2ln⁡(ert1)=ln⁡2rt1=ln⁡2t1=ln⁡2r(∗)

We now need to calculate r. We're told that the price of the good tripled after the first six years. Therefore, P(6)=3P0⇒P0e6r=3P0.

We solve this equation for r, as follows: P0e6r=3P0P0e6r=3P0e6r=3ln⁡(e6r)=ln⁡(3)r=ln⁡36

Finally, substituting this into (∗) and evaluating, we get t1=ln⁡2r=ln⁡2(ln⁡36)=6ln⁡2ln⁡3≈3.8, rounded to one decimal place.
